beginner.summary: For developers, testers and junior DevOps engineers who can use Git and the command line but have not built pipelines on CircleCI. Covers connecting a repository through the CircleCI GitHub App or OAuth integration, the version 2.1 config.yml format, jobs, steps and the Docker and machine executors with cimg convenience images, workflows with requires and branch and tag filters, environment variables and pipeline values, dependency caching, workspaces, artifacts and test results, service containers, resource classes and credits, certified orbs, contexts, approval jobs, building Docker images with setup_remote_docker, the local CircleCI CLI and SSH debugging, ending with a complete pipeline capstone for a Node.js API.
prerequisites: Uses Git daily: cloning, branching, committing, pushing and opening pull requests on GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket
Reads and edits YAML files and runs shell commands such as npm, pip or make in a Linux terminal
Has a GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket account with admin rights on a practice repository, a free CircleCI account and Docker installed locally
outcomes: Connect a repository to CircleCI and write a valid version 2.1 config.yml with jobs, steps, executors and workflows
Speed up and structure pipelines with dependency caches, workspaces, artifacts, test results and service containers
Manage configuration and secrets with environment variables, pipeline values, contexts, orbs and approval jobs
Diagnose failed jobs with the CircleCI CLI, step output and SSH reruns, and build and push a Docker image from a pipeline
